title: Combine Auditable and Cacheable markers
description: Two marker interfaces — Auditable and Cacheable — independently tag classes for different behaviours. AuditLogger logs only Auditable objects. ResponseCache stores and retrieves only Cacheable objects, returning null for unmarked ones. Some classes implement both, some one, some neither. Wire up the markers on the provided domain classes and complete both services.
hints: A class can implement multiple marker interfaces at once
AuditLogger checks 'instanceof Auditable'; ResponseCache checks 'instanceof Cacheable'
The two markers are completely independent — implementing one does not affect the other
issues: Without markers, each service needs its own hard-coded allowlist of supported types
Classes that need both behaviours would have to be registered in two separate places
overallGoal: Use two independent marker interfaces so classes can opt in to auditing, caching, both, or neither — and each service responds only to its own marker.
goals: Define Auditable and Cacheable as separate marker interfaces with no methods
Apply each marker to the appropriate classes
In each service, use instanceof to check for the relevant marker before processing
